ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r12.claim: One view excuses mistaken attribution before the prohibition, but Abu Hayyan rejects it because conduct before the rule cannot be called an error.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r12.anchor: فيما أخطأتم به، قيل: رفع الحرج عنهم فيما كان قبل النهي، وهذا ضعيف لا يوصف بالخطأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r13.claim: Another view excuses a slip of the tongue, accidental or affectionate, such as calling a child “son” or an elder “father.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: فيما سبق إليه اللسان. إما على سبيل الغلط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r14.claim: Only deliberate attribution incurs blame; God forgives deliberate offenders who repent and lifts blame for mistakes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p452#2/r14.anchor: وكان الله غفورا للعامد إذا تاب، رحيما حيث رفع الجناح عن المخطئ

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p159/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p159/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p159/r4.claim: Adopted children must be attributed to their actual fathers; if a father is unknown, the child is an ally and brother, not a son.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p159/r4.anchor: Muslims are directed to attribute adopted children to their actual fathers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p159/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p159/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p159/r5.claim: Past adoption practices under jāhiliyyah are forgiven, but after this clarification Muslims may no longer cling to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p159/r5.anchor: Whatever has happened till then under the influence of jāhiliyyah has been forgiven by God

RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r1.claim: The guidance is to call adopted children by their fathers' names, which places things in their proper position and is more just.
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : { ادعوهم لآبائهم } أرشد وقال : { هو أقسط عند الله }

RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r2.claim: Aqsaṭ may omit its comparison and mean more just than all speech, like the unqualified expression God is greater; alternatively, the earlier practice is understood, meaning more just than calling them sons of so-and-so.
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r2.anchor: أن يكون ترك الإضافة للعموم أي أعدل كل كلام

RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r3.claim: When their fathers are unknown, call them brothers in religion; if they are freed persons, call them the client of so-and-so.
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r3.anchor: يعني قولوا لهم إخواننا وأخو فلان فإن كانوا محررين فقولوا مولى فلان

RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r4.claim: There is no blame for inadvertent forms of address such as calling someone my son out of affection or my father out of respect; these are like an unintentional oath or a slip of the tongue.
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r4.anchor: فكذلك سبق اللسان في قول القائل ابني والسهو في قوله ابني من غير قصد إلى إثبات النسب سواء

RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r5.claim: The phrase about what hearts intend is a subject whose omitted predicate is recovered from the preceding clause: deliberate intent incurs blame.
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r5.anchor: مبتدأ خبره محذوف يدل عليه ما سبق وهو الجناح

RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r6.claim: A slip or unintentional use of son without intending to establish lineage is equivalent to a mistake, while deliberate intent incurs sin.
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r6.anchor: سبق اللسان في قول القائل ابني والسهو في قوله ابني من غير قصد إلى إثبات النسب سواء

RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r7.claim: Forgiveness is a powerful person's covering or removing a wrong by someone under his power; a servant who conceals a master's fault from fear is not thereby forgiving him.
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r7.anchor: المغفرة هو أن يسترد القادر القبيح الصادر ممن تحت قدرته حتى أن العبد إذا ستر عيب سيده

RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r8.claim: Mercy is kindness to someone because of their helplessness and without compensation; kindness to a powerful person, for expected benefit, or in repayment of prior kindness is not mercy in this strict sense.
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r8.anchor: الرحمة هو أن يميل إليه بالإحسان لعجز المرحوم إليه لا لعوض

RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r9.claim: When forgiveness precedes mercy, God first covers the wrong, then sees the servant's helplessness and gives what suffices; when forgiveness follows mercy, He first favors the helpless and then withholds punishment and covers sins.
RAZI-FULL:v25p168/r9.anchor: فالمغفرة إذا ذكرت قبل الرحمة يكون معناها أنه ستر عيبه ثم رآه مفلسا عاجزا فرحمه

STUDYQURAN:33:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r1.speaker: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says Muslims formerly called Zayd ibn Ḥārithah “Zayd ibn Muhammad” until this revelation instructed them to name adopted children after their fathers.
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r1.anchor: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar is reported to have said, “We did not use to call Zayd ibn Ḥārithah by any name other than Zayd ibn Muhammad

STUDYQURAN:33:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r2.claim: The verse ends the pre-Islamic practice of adopting others as the Prophet adopted Zayd and directs Muslims to relate instead as brothers and clients.
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r2.anchor: This verse abolished the pre-Islamic custom of adopting others the way the Prophet had adopted Zayd

STUDYQURAN:33:5/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r3.claim: “Clients” translates mawālī, plural of mawlā, a term used for heirs, God as Master, and varied close relationships; mawlā is etymologically related to walī, protector or protecting friend.
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r3.anchor: Clients translates mawālī (sing. mawlā), which is elsewhere translated heirs

STUDYQURAN:33:5/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r4.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r4.claim: Those who practiced adoption as the Prophet did with Zayd are not blamed because they did not intend to oppose God's will.
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r4.anchor: There is no blame upon those who had engaged in the practice of adoption as the Prophet did in Zayd’s case

STUDYQURAN:33:5/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r5.claim: More broadly, people are not held accountable for unintended mistakes.
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r5.anchor: Applied more broadly, this verse is understood to mean that people are not taken to account for unintended mistakes

STUDYQURAN:33:5/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r6.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r6.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that God exempts his community from mistakes, forgetfulness, and acts done under compulsion.
STUDYQURAN:33:5/r6.anchor: the Prophet is reported to have said, “God exonerates my community of being mistaken, of forgetting, and of that which they are forced to do”

BURSEVI:v7p104/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r1.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p104/r1.claim: Kashf al-asrar says naming adopted children after their actual fathers is more just and truthful than calling them by other fathers.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r1.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" : هو أعدل وأصدق من دعائهم إياهم لغير آبائهم

BURSEVI:v7p104/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p104/r2.claim: Some grammarians say that when a conditional sense is impossible, an becomes idh, a particle of past time; thus the past and future forms here do not conflict.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم متى عرض ما يحيل معنى الشرط جعلت أن بمعنى إذ وإذ يكون للماضي

BURSEVI:v7p104/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r3.speaker: البيضاوي
BURSEVI:v7p104/r3.claim: Al-Baydawi explains that lam turns the present verb into a past form and joins it to itself, so the conditional particle governs the combined phrase as if it meant if you left the act.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r3.anchor: قال البيضاوي في قوله تعالى : {فإن لم تفعلوا} (البقرة : 24) إن تفعلوا جزم بلم

BURSEVI:v7p104/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104/r4.claim: If their fathers are unknown, those who have accepted Islam are religious brothers and allies; they should be addressed as brother or mawla in religious affection.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r4.anchor: أي : فهم إخوانكم في الدين يعني من أسلم منهم {ومواليكم} وأولياؤكم فيه

BURSEVI:v7p104/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104/r5.claim: Abu Hudhayfa had freed and adopted Salim, who had been called Salim ibn Abi Hudhayfa; after this verse, he was called the mawla of Abu Hudhayfa.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r5.anchor: أن أبا حذيفة أعتق عبدا يقال له سالم وتبناه وكانوا يسمونه سالم ابن أبي حذيفة

BURSEVI:v7p104/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104/r6.claim: Janah means sin: as a ship leans toward one side, sin inclines a person away from the truth; the term then came to mean any sin.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r6.anchor: يقال جنحت السفينة أي : مالت إلى أحد جانبيها وسمي الإثم المائل بالإنسان على الحق جناحا

BURSEVI:v7p104/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p104/r7.claim: Some derive janah from Persian gunah by the Arabic habit of substituting sounds, as with jawhar from gohar.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنه معرب كناه على ما هو عادة العرب في الإبدال ومثله الجوهر معرب كوهر

BURSEVI:v7p104/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104/r8.claim: The hamza in akhta'tum is a hamzat al-qat' because the if'al verb form has a pronounced hamza.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r8.anchor: بقطع الهمزة لأن همزة باب الأفعال مقطوعة

BURSEVI:v7p104/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104/r9.claim: The pardon covers mistaken naming before the prohibition, slips of the tongue, and forgetfulness.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r9.anchor: فيما فعلتموه من ذلك مخطئين قبل النهي أو بعده على سبق اللسان أو النسيان

BURSEVI:v7p104/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
BURSEVI:v7p104/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya says naming counts as an error only after the prohibition; khata' is deviation from the proper direction.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : لا تتصف التسمية بالخطأ إلا بعد النهي والخطأ العدول عن الجهة

BURSEVI:v7p104/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
BURSEVI:v7p104/r11.claim: Ibn Atiyya distinguishes one who knowingly does wrong as khati from one unaware of the error as mukhti, with usage examples and the verse about none eating except sinners.
BURSEVI:v7p104/r11.anchor: وفرق بين الخاطىء والمخطيء فإن من يأتي بالخطى وهو يعلم أنه خطأ فهو خاطىء

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r1.claim: The phrase is glossed in Persian as concerning that in which you made an error.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r1.anchor: والمعنى بالفارسية : (دران يزى كه خطا كرديد بآن)

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r2.claim: One parsing makes ma genitive, coordinated with the earlier ma; another makes it a nominative subject with an omitted predicate, assigning liability to deliberate intent.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r2.anchor: على أن ما محل الجر عطفا على ما أخطأتم أو ما تعمدت قلوبكم فيه الجناح

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r3.claim: Liability attaches to what the heart deliberately intended after the prohibition.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r3.anchor: أي : ولكن الجناح فيما قصدت قلوبكم بعد النهي

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r4.speaker: حديث
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r4.claim: A hadith warns that anyone who knowingly claims a father other than his own is forbidden Paradise.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من دعي إلى غير أبيه وهو يعلم أنه غير أبيه فالجنة عليه حرام"

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r5.claim: God is abundant in forgiveness and mercy, forgiving error and showing mercy.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r5.anchor: بليغ المغفرة والرحمة يغفر لخطيئتي ويرحم

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r6.speaker: عمر
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r6.claim: Umar heard a man ask God to forgive his sins and answered that one should seek the All-Subduing's forgiveness, since error has already been overlooked.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r6.anchor: وسمع عمر رضي الله عنه رجلا يقول : اللهم اغفر خطاياي فقال : يا ابن آدم استغفر الصمد

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r7.claim: This does not contradict the verse: a mistaken person who was negligent and entered into causes leading to the error may still be a fit object of forgiveness and mercy.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r7.anchor: هذا لا يخالف الآية لأن المخطىء إذا قصر ووقع في أسباب أدته إلى الخطأ

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r8.claim: If an adopter claims as son a person of unknown lineage who is younger than himself, lineage is established; if the person is his slave, he is freed with the established lineage.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r8.anchor: إذا كان مجهول النسب وأصغر سنا من المتبني ثبت نسبه منه وإن كان عبدا له عتق

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r9.claim: If the adopter is too old to be the claimed child's father, lineage is not established, but Abu Hanifa frees the slave.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r9.anchor: وإن كان لا يولد لمثله لم يثبت النسب ولكنه يعتق عند أبي حنيفة

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r10.speaker: صاحبا أبي حنيفة
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa's two companions disagree: the slave is not freed because an impossible statement is void.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r10.anchor: خلافا لصاحبيه فإنه لا يعتق عندهما لأن كلامه محال فيلغو

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r11.claim: Adoption does not establish new lineage for someone already known to have another lineage, though if he is the adopter's slave he is freed.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r11.anchor: وأما معروف النسب فلا يثبت نسبه بالتبني وإن كان عبدا عتق

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r12.claim: Denying the lineage of an adopted child incurs no liability, but denying an established biological child entails li'an for accusing one's wife; retracting the accusation brings a hadd.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r12.anchor: واعلم أن من نفى نسب الدعي عنه لا يلزمه شيء إذ هو ليس بابن له حقيقة

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r13.speaker: حديث
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r13.claim: A hadith says every lineage and noble standing will end except the Prophet's lineage and noble standing.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r13.anchor: كما قال : "كل حسب ونسب ينقطع إلا حسبي ونسبي"

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r14.claim: The enduring true lineage is connection to the Prophet through poverty and prophethood; one must not sever that bond by abandoning his Sunnah and way.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r14.anchor: فحسبه الفقر ونسبه النبوة فينبغي أن لا يقطع الرحم عن النبوة بترك سنته وسيرته

BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r15.claim: Breaking figurative family ties may be preferable when maintaining them would lead to disbelief or sin.
BURSEVI:v7p104#2/r15.anchor: إذ ربما يقطع الرحم المجازي إذا كان الوصل مؤديا إلى الكفر أو المعصية

TAB-FULL:v19p12/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p12/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p12/r1.claim: Adopted sons must be attributed to their biological fathers; Muhammad is told to call Zayd the son of Ḥāritha, not his own son.
TAB-FULL:v19p12/r1.anchor: انسبوا أدعياءكم الذين ألحقتم أنسابهم بكم لآبائهم. يقول لنبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم: ألحق نسب زيد بأبيه حارثة، ولا تدعه زيد ابن محمد

TAB-FULL:v19p12#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p12#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p12#2/r1.claim: Calling adopted sons by their fathers’ names is more just, truthful, and correct than attributing them to adoptive claimants who are not their fathers.
TAB-FULL:v19p12#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله " {ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله} [الأحزاب: 5] أي أعدل عند الله

TAB-FULL:v19p12#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p12#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p12#2/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses aqsat as more just before God.
TAB-FULL:v19p12#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله " {ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله} [الأحزاب: 5] أي أعدل عند الله

TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r1.claim: If the fathers of adopted sons are unknown, they cannot be assigned to the men who adopted them.
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r1.anchor: {فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم} [الأحزاب: 5]

TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r2.claim: Those whose fathers are unknown count as brothers in religion if they share the faith, and as clients or freedmen, not sons.
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r2.anchor: {فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم} [الأحزاب: 5]

TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī links the designation as brothers in religion to the same wording in 9:11.
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r3.anchor: {فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم} [الأحزاب: 5]

TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r4.claim: Qatada says naming adopted sons after their fathers is more just; if the father is unknown, the person is a brother and client.
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، " {ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله} [الأحزاب: 5] أي أعدل عند الله

TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r5.speaker: أبو بكرة
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r5.claim: Abu Bakra says his own father is unknown, yet he belongs among the believers’ brothers in religion.
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r5.anchor: قال أبو بكرة: قال الله {ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم

TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r6.speaker: أبو بكرة عن أبيه
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r6.claim: Abu Bakra’s father said that, if Abu Bakra knew his father was a donkey, he would still affiliate himself to him.
TAB-FULL:v19p12#3/r6.anchor: قال أبي: والله إني لأظنه لو علم أن أباه كان حمارا لانتمى إليه

TAB-FULL:v19p13/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r1.claim: There is no blame for mistakenly assigning someone to a father when one believes that man is his father.

TAB-FULL:v19p13/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r2.claim: Blame applies when someone knowingly assigns a person to a man who is not his father.

TAB-FULL:v19p13/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r3.claim: Qatada distinguishes an assumed but mistaken attribution, which God does not charge, from a deliberate attribution to someone other than the known father.
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، " {وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به} [الأحزاب: 5] يقول: إذا دعوت الرجل لغير أبيه وأنت ترى أنه كذلك

TAB-FULL:v19p13/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r4.claim: Mujahid says deliberate action means what is done after clarification and prohibition, here and elsewhere.
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {تعمدت قلوبكم} [الأحزاب: 5] قال: فالعمد ما أتى بعد البيان والنهي في هذا وغيره

TAB-FULL:v19p13/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r5.claim: The second ما is genitive by coordination with the ما in فيما; the sense is no blame for error, but blame for deliberate action.
TAB-FULL:v19p13/r5.anchor: وما التي في قوله {ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم} [الأحزاب: 5] خفض ردا على ما التي في قوله {فيما أخطأتم به} [الأحزاب: 5]

TAB-FULL:v1p18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī uses the rule to call people by their fathers' names as an analogy: lineage is exclusive, whereas language use can belong to multiple peoples.
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r1.anchor: لقول الله تعالى ذكره: {ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله}

TAB-FULL:v1p18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r2.claim: He reads 'from every tongue' to mean that a word shared in form and meaning by Arabic and other peoples belongs to each language, without one having exclusive claim.
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r2.anchor: فيه من كل لسان، اتفق فيه لفظ العرب ولفظ غيرها من الأمم التي تنطق به

TAB-FULL:v1p18/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r3.claim: A region between plain and mountain, or land and sea, can truthfully be described by both qualities; naming one does not cancel the other, just as a word can belong to two languages.
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r3.anchor: كما لو أن أرضا بين سهل وجبل، لها هواء السهل وهواء الجبل، أو بين بر وبحر، لها هواء البر وهواء البحر

TAB-FULL:v1p18/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the claim that 'from every tongue' means some Qur'anic expressions are non-Arabic and cannot properly be ascribed to Arabic, since God calls the Qur'an Arabic.
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r4.anchor: فبين إذا خطأ قول من زعم أن القائل من السلف: في القرآن من كل لسان، إنما عنى بقيله ذلك

TAB-FULL:v1p18/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r5.claim: He challenges the theory that foreign peoples' terms were borrowed into Arabic: the reverse, Arabic terms spreading to other peoples, is equally possible, and the opponent must supply proof distinguishing them.
TAB-FULL:v1p18/r5.anchor: ما برهانك على صحة ما قلت في ذلك من الوجه الذي يجب التسليم له؟ فقد علمت من خالفك

TABATABAI:33:4-6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r3.claim: The lām indicates specification: calling adopted children to their fathers means attributing them to those fathers.
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r3.anchor: للاختصاص أي ادعوهم وهم مخصوصون بآبائهم

TABATABAI:33:4-6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r4.claim: The pronoun in huwa aqsaṭ refers to the verbal noun implied by “call them,” as in 5:8; aqsaṭ is comparative from qisṭ, justice.
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r4.anchor: صيغة تفضيل من القسط بمعنى العدل

TABATABAI:33:4-6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r5.claim: Attributing them to their fathers is the more just course before God.
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r5.anchor: لأن الدعاء لآبائهم أعدل عند الله

TABATABAI:33:4-6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r6.claim: Not knowing their fathers means not knowing their identities; do not invent lineage, but address them as brothers and allies in religion.
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r6.anchor: المراد بعدم علمهم آباءهم عدم معرفتهم بأعيانهم

TABATABAI:33:4-6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r7.claim: Mawālī here means allies or guardians.
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r7.anchor: عدم معرفتهم بأعيانهم، والموالي هم الأولياء

TABATABAI:33:4-6/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r8.claim: There is no sin for mistaken attribution through lapse or forgetfulness, but deliberate false attribution is sinful; God's forgiveness here concerns the mistake.
TABATABAI:33:4-6/r8.anchor: أي لا ذنب لكم في الذي أخطأتم به لسهو أو نسيان

TABRISI:33:4-5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:4-5/r5.claim: Children should be attributed to their biological fathers, or to the men whose marital beds they were born in.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r5.anchor: الذين ولدوهم وانسبوهم إليهم أو إلى من ولدوا على فراشهم

TABRISI:33:4-5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:4-5/r6.claim: Attributing people to their real fathers is the fairest statement and judgment before God.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r6.anchor: أي أعدل عند الله قولا وحكما

TABRISI:33:4-5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
TABRISI:33:4-5/r7.claim: Ibn Umar said they called Zayd ibn Haritha Zayd ibn Muhammad until this verse was revealed; al-Bukhari recorded the report in his Sahih.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r7.anchor: وروى سالم عن ابن عمر قال:

TABRISI:33:4-5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:4-5/r8.claim: When their fathers' identities are unknown, call them brothers in the faith.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r8.anchor: أي لم تعرفوا بأعيانهم { فإخوانكم في الدين }

TABRISI:33:4-5/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:4-5/r9.claim: He explains mawali here as paternal cousins.

TABRISI:33:4-5/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r10.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:33:4-5/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows mawali to mean allies in religion, who owe one another support.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r10.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون المراد أوليائكم في الدين

TABRISI:33:4-5/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:4-5/r11.claim: Another explanation is that mawali are the freedmen of people who emancipated them, to whom their wala belongs.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r11.anchor: وقيل: معناه معتقوكم ومحرروكم إذا اعتقتموهم من رق فلكم ولاؤهم.

TABRISI:33:4-5/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:4-5/r12.claim: There is no blame for mistakenly attributing someone to an adoptive father when one believes he is the biological father and does not know otherwise.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r12.anchor: في نسبته إلى المتبني إذا ظننتم أنه أبوه ولم تعلموا أنه ليس بابن له

TABRISI:33:4-5/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:4-5/r13.claim: People are accountable for deliberately attributing someone to someone other than his father.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r13.anchor: في الذي تعمدته قلوبكم وقصدتموه من دعائهم إلى غير آبائهم

TABRISI:33:4-5/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r14.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:33:4-5/r14.claim: Mujahid distinguishes mistakes made before the prohibition from deliberate attribution after it.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r14.anchor: ما أخطأتم قبل النهي وما تعمدتموه بعد النهي عن مجاهد

TABRISI:33:4-5/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:4-5/r15.claim: God forgives what people said before and is merciful to them.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r15.anchor: لما سلف من قولكم { رحيما } بكم

TABRISI:33:4-5/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:4-5/r16.claim: The verse establishes that claiming a lineage to someone other than one's father is impermissible; the Sunnah strongly warns against it.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r16.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أنه لا يجوز الانتساب إلى غير الأب وقد وردت السنة

TABRISI:33:4-5/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:4-5/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:4-5/r17.claim: A Sunnah report curses whoever claims a father or patron other than his own.
TABRISI:33:4-5/r17.anchor: من انتسب إلى غير أبيه أو انتمى إلى غير مواليه فعليه لعنة الله

THALABI:v8p7/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p7/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p7/r2.claim: The passage was revealed after Zayd, whom Muhammad had freed and adopted before revelation, married Zaynab, Zayd’s former wife; Jews and hypocrites objected that Muhammad married his son’s wife.
THALABI:v8p7/r2.anchor: نزلت في زيد بن حارثة بن شراحيل الكلبي من بني عبد ود، كان عبدا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأعتقه وتبناه قبل الوحي

THALABI:v8p7/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p7/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p7/r4.claim: Call adopted people by their birth fathers; this is more just. If their fathers are unknown, regard them as brothers in faith and freed clients, not sons.
THALABI:v8p7/r4.anchor: فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم

THALABI:v8p7/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p7/r5.speaker: أبو بكر
THALABI:v8p7/r5.claim: Abu Bakr says that, since he does not know his father, he is among the believers’ brothers in religion.
THALABI:v8p7/r5.anchor: قال أبو بكر: قال الله تعالى: ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين

THALABI:v8p7/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p7/r6.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p7/r6.claim: Qatada says there is no blame for mistakenly assigning someone to another father before the prohibition, when one believed the attribution was true.
THALABI:v8p7/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: يعني أن تدعوه لغير أبيه وهو يرى أنه كذلك

THALABI:v8p7/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p7/r7.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p7/r7.claim: Qatada says blame attaches to knowingly assigning someone to another father after the prohibition.
THALABI:v8p7/r7.anchor: ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم فنسبتموه إلى غير أبيه بعد النهي، وأنتم تعلمون أنه ليس بابنه

THALABI:v8p7/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p7/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p7/r8.claim: The second “ما” is genitive by coordination with the “ما” in “فيما أخطأتم به”; the sense is “but in what your hearts intended.”
THALABI:v8p7/r8.anchor: ومحل ما في قوله: ما تعمدت قلوبكم خفض ردا على (ما) التي في قوله: فيما أخطأتم به

THALABI:v8p7/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p7/r9.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v8p7/r9.claim: The Prophet says that anyone who claims descent from someone other than his father or patron is cursed by God, angels, and all people.
THALABI:v8p7/r9.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من ادعى إلى غير أبيه أو إلى غير أهل نعمته فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين»

THALABI:v8p7/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p7/r10.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v8p7/r10.claim: Aisha reports that Abu Hudhayfa adopted Salim, a freedman of an Ansari woman, and the old practice let adopted sons inherit until the verse required attribution to their fathers.
THALABI:v8p7/r10.anchor: عن عائشة أن أبا حذيفة بن عتبة بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس- كان ممن شهد بدرا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم- تبنى سالما وأنكحه ابنة أخيه هند بنت الوليد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the command as attributing people to the fathers who begot them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: انسبوهم إلى آبائهم الذين ولدوهم (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r2.claim: When their fathers are unknown, they are your brothers in religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r2.anchor: أي: فهم إخوانكم في الدين. قال ابن عباس:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas begins to explain the brothers in religion as those of you who accepted Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد من أسلم [منكم]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، المبرد والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Mubarrad, and al-Zajjaj take mawālī as paternal cousins; al-Mubarrad cites a line addressing cousins as mawālī as evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r1.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس (¬7)، واختيار المبرد (¬8) والزجاج (¬9). وأنشد المبرد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj offers an alternative: mawālī may mean your allies or protectors in religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: يجوز أن يكون ومواليكم أولياؤكم في الدين (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r3.claim: Another view takes mawālī as freedmen: a man who was a slave and was emancipated is his master's mawlā, as Zayd ibn Haritha was the Prophet's mawlā; Muqatil's wording supports this.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: يعني بالموالي المعتقين أي: إن كان عبدا وأعتقه فهو مولاك، كما كان زيد بن حارثة مولى النبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r4.claim: Mujahid and Muqatil say the excused mistake includes what people said before the prohibition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد ومقاتل: يعني فيما قلتموه قبل النهي (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r5.claim: Qatada says there is no blame for calling someone by the wrong father's name when one believes that name is correct.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: لو دعوت رجلا لغير أبيه وأنت ترى أنه أبوه لم يكن عليك بأس (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r6.claim: On this explanation, the verse excuses an unintentional error in a person's lineage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r6.anchor: فعلى هذا الخطاب أن يخطئ في نسبه من غير تعمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq gives a third view: a mistaken designation is excused if the speaker does not deliberately treat the person as a child for inheritance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p172#2/r7.anchor: وذكر أبو إسحاق قولا ثالثا فقال: ويجوز أن يكون: (ولا جناح عليكم في أن تقولوا بما هي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p173/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p173/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p173/r1.claim: God's forgiveness and mercy concern what people said before the prohibition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p173/r1.anchor: لما كان من قولكم (¬7) قبل النهي رحيما بكم.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r5.claim: Adopted children should be attributed to the fathers who begot them; this is more just before God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r5.anchor: { ادعوهم لآبائهم } أي: انسبوهم إلى الذين ولدوهم { هو أقسط عند الله } أعدل عند الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r6.claim: If their fathers are unknown, they are brothers in religion and your mawālī, meaning paternal cousins.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r6.anchor: { فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم } من هم { فإخوانكم في الدين } أي فهم إخوانكم في الدين { ومواليكم } وبنو عمكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r7.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r7.claim: Another explanation of mawālī is your allies in religion.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r7.anchor: وبنو عمكم. وقيل: أولياؤكم في الدين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r8.claim: There is no blame for an inadvertent form of address, such as calling someone “my son” without intending inheritance as if he were a biological child; blame attaches to what the heart intends.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:4-5/r8.anchor: وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به } وهو ن يقول لغير ابنه: يا بني

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698/r7.claim: Calling them by their fathers' names is more equitable before God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698/r7.anchor: {ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله} [الأحزاب: 5] أعدل عند الله

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddī explains mawālī here as clients whom one has freed.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r2.claim: Yaḥyā says to call the person our client so-and-so and our brother so-and-so.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r2.anchor: قال يحيى: قولوا ولينا فلان، وأخونا فلان

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r3.claim: Someone who, after the prohibition, forgetfully names an adoptee after the adoptive father commits no sin.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r3.anchor: إن أخطأ الرجل بعد النهي فنسبه إلى الذي تبناه ناسيا، فليس عليه في ذلك إثم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the intentional act to be deliberately calling them by someone other than the fathers God assigned them to.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r4.anchor: أن تدعوهم إلى غير آبائهم الذين ألحقهم الله بهم متعمدين لذلك وهذا تفسير الحسن

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the excuse for error covers this and other matters before the prohibition, while deliberate conduct concerns the period after it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به} [الأحزاب: 5] قبل النهي عن هذا وغيره

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r6.speaker: سعد بن مالك
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r6.claim: Saʿd ibn Mālik reports the Prophet's warning that knowingly claiming another man as one's father bars one from Paradise; Abū Bakra confirmed hearing it too.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p698#2/r6.anchor: عن سعد بن مالك قال: سمعت أذناي ووعى قلبي من محمد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

ELMALILI:33:4-5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r10.claim: Adopted children must be attributed to their fathers; keeping each person's lineage distinct is truthful, just, and better for public welfare.
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r10.anchor: Onları babalarına çağırın: babalarına nisbet edin

ELMALILI:33:4-5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r11.claim: When their fathers are unknown, the people are brothers in religion and allies, not relatives by lineage.

ELMALILI:33:4-5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r12.claim: There is no blame for unintentional mistakes, whether made before or after the prohibition, including slips and forgetfulness.
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r12.anchor: kasdınız olmaksızın sehv ü nisyan ile yaptığınız yanlışlıklarda

ELMALILI:33:4-5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r13.claim: Sin attaches to what the heart deliberately intends.
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r13.anchor: velâkin kalblerinizin ta‘ammüd ettiği, işte günah ondadır

ELMALILI:33:4-5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r14.claim: God is forgiving and merciful, forgiving the person who errs.
ELMALILI:33:4-5/r14.anchor: Allah bir Gafûr, Rahîm bulunuyor hata edeni affeder.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r2.claim: The saying that God made no two hearts in a person’s chest introduces and grounds the coming discussion of pagan customs and hypocrites as opposed to nature and reality, including the impossibility of having two gods or religions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r2.anchor: Gelecek âyetlerde bazı Câhiliye âdetleriyle münafıklardan söz edileceği, bu âdetlerin fıtrata ve gerçekliğe ters düştüğü, bir kimsenin iki tanrısı ve iki dini olamayacağı ifade edileceği için bunlara bir giriş ve dayanak olmak üzere vecize değerindeki şu cümleye yer verilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r7.claim: Adopting a child cannot change the child’s lineage: just as a person has one heart, A’s child cannot thereby become B’s child; this is a law of nature and human disposition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r7.anchor: Bir göğüste iki kalbin olmaması nasıl bir tabiat kanunu ise A’nın çocuğunun evlât edinme yoluyla B’nin çocuğu olamayacağı da bir fıtrat ve tabiat kanunudur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r8.claim: Changing an adopted child’s lineage conflicts with Islamic rules on covering, marriage and maḥram status, parent-child relations, reciprocal rights and duties, and inheritance; living as a full family member in a non-relative household also conflicts with these rules.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r8.anchor: İslâm’ın koyduğu örtünme vecibesi, evlenme imkânı veya yasağı, çocuk-ebeveyn ilişkisi, karşılıklı haklar ve ödevler, miras gibi konulara dair kurallar da, çocuklarla gerçek ana babalarının soy bağlarının kesilip değiştirilmesine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r9.claim: As social and moral reform reached adoption, the command to name children after their fathers ended the practice of attaching adopted children to another lineage.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r9.anchor: Yapılmakta olan sosyal ve ahlâkî ıslahat içinde sıra bu âdetin kaldırılmasına gelmiş, “...babalarının soy adları ile anın” emri ile bu uygulamaya son verilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r10.speaker: Tefsir kitapları
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r10.claim: Tafsir books say Zayd ibn Ḥāritha’s case occasioned the verse: abducted and enslaved as a child, he was freed and adopted by Muhammad, chose to stay with him over his birth family, and was renamed from Zayd ibn Muhammad to Zayd ibn Ḥāritha after the revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r10.anchor: Tefsir kitaplarında bu münasebetle Hz. Peygamber’in evlâtlığı Zeyd b. Hârise’den söz edilir ve âyetin inişine onun bu durumunun sebep olduğu söylenir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r11.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r11.claim: The Prophet promised to be beside a person who takes an orphan into their care in Paradise, like two adjacent fingers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r11.anchor: Kimsesiz çocukları koruması altına alan kimse ile ben, cennette yan yana iki parmak gibi beraber olacağım

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r12.claim: Caring for children in need is meritorious and honorable, but no one may erase their lineage or birth parents, add them to legal heirs, or treat them as biological children regarding maḥram rules; Islam recommends care and support while treating them as religious siblings under legal and lawful-unlawful rules.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:4/r12.anchor: Ancak bunu yapmak için çocuğun kendi soy kütüğü ile ilişkisini kesmek, öz ana babasını unutturmak kimsenin hakkı olmadığı gibi

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p171#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p171#2/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p171#2/r1.claim: Ibn Umar says they used to call Zayd ibn Haritha “Zayd ibn Muhammad” until the command to call adopted sons by their fathers was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p171#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال ما كنا ندعو زيد بن حارثة إلا زيد بن محمد جتى نزل في القرآن

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p352/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p352/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p352/r1.claim: The passage was revealed over the adoption of Zayd ibn Haritha and accusations by Jews and hypocrites that the Prophet had married his adopted son’s former wife, Zaynab.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p352/r1.anchor: نزلت في زيد بن حارثة كان عبدا لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فأعتقه

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p352/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p352/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p352/r2.claim: Ibn Umar says they used to call Zayd ibn Haritha Zayd ibn Muhammad until this verse was revealed; al-Wahidi notes al-Bukhari transmitted the report.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p352/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر أنه كان يقول: ما كنا ندعو زيد بن حارثة

AKHFASH:v2p480/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p480/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p480/r2.claim: The preposition li- follows the passive idea because Arabic says huwa yudʿā li-fulān, he is called after so-and-so.
AKHFASH:v2p480/r2.anchor: وقال {ادعوهم لآبائهم} لأنك تقول "هو يدعى لفلان"

DAMGHANI:v1p498/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p498/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p498/r2.claim: Mawālī can mean a freed person, the one whom someone has emancipated from slavery.
DAMGHANI:v1p498/r2.anchor: التاسع المولى المعتق قوله تعالى في سورة الأحزاب

FARRA:v1p142/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p142/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p142/r1.claim: In ‘then your brothers and clients,’ the nouns can be nominative as a predicate; they can instead be accusative with an implicit verb ‘call them.’
FARRA:v1p142/r1.anchor: فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم» ولو نصبت هاهنا على إضمار فعل (ادعوهم إخوانكم ومواليكم)

FARRA:v1p142/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p142/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p142/r3.claim: A following noun is nominative when ‘it is’ can be supplied before it; otherwise it continues the preceding verb, with accusative examples such as buying good food or wearing white.
FARRA:v1p142/r3.anchor: وإنما يرفع من ذا ما كان اسما يحسن فيه «هو» مع المرفوع. فإذا لم يحسن فيه «هو» أجريته على ما قبله

FARRA:v2p335/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p335/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p335/r2.claim: Adopted sons must be attributed to their biological fathers.
FARRA:v2p335/r2.anchor: ثم أمرهم فقال: ادعوهم لآبائهم [5] أي انسبوهم إلى آبائهم

FARRA:v2p335/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p335/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p335/r3.claim: When their fathers are unknown, attribute them to their patrons, for example as so-and-so son of ʿAbd Allāh or ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
FARRA:v2p335/r3.anchor: فانسبوهم إلى نسبة مواليكم الذين لا تعرفون آباءهم: فلان بن عبد الله

FARRA:v2p335/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p335/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p335/r4.claim: There is no blame for unintended mistakes; sin concerns deliberate acts, and the second mā is genitive by coordination with the mā in fīmā.
FARRA:v2p335/r4.anchor: فيما لم تقصدوا له من الخطأ، إنما الإثم فيما تعمدتم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p348#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p348#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p348#3/r1.claim: Aqsat means more just and more correct.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p348#3/r1.anchor: {هو أقسط عند الله} أي أعدل وأصح.

MAJAZ:v2p134/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p134/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p134/r1.claim: He glosses the phrase as your brothers in the religious community.
MAJAZ:v2p134/r1.anchor: أي إخوانكم فى الملة وخرج مخرج فتى والجميع

MAJAZ:v2p134/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p134/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p134/r2.claim: He notes the related noun fatā has the plural forms fityān and fitya.
MAJAZ:v2p134/r2.anchor: وخرج مخرج فتى والجميع فتيان وفتية

MAJAZ:v2p134/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p134/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p134/r3.claim: Mawālīkum means your paternal cousins and your patrons or guardians.

NAHHAS:v3p302/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p302/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p302/r1.claim: Those whose fathers are unknown are your brothers in religion and your clients; mawālī is coordinated with ikhwa.

NAHHAS:v3p302/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p302/r2.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v3p302/r2.claim: Qatāda explains error as attributing a man to someone other than his father while believing that person really is his father.
NAHHAS:v3p302/r2.anchor: قول قتادة هو أن ينسب الرجل إلى غير أبيه وهو يرى أنه أبوه

NAHHAS:v3p302/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p302/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p302/r3.claim: Another explanation generalizes the exemption to anything done by mistake; ʿAṭāʾ ruled that someone who unknowingly takes glass for payment or greets an unrecognized person does not incur liability or break an oath.
NAHHAS:v3p302/r3.anchor: وقد قيل إن هذا مجمل أي وليس عليكم جناح في شيء أخطأتم به وكانت فتيا عطاء على هذا

NAHHAS:v3p302/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p302/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p302/r4.claim: Mā may be genitive, coordinated with the mā governed by bi in the preceding phrase, or nominative after an implied subject: what you are held accountable for is what your hearts intended.
NAHHAS:v3p302/r4.anchor: ما في موضع خفض ردا على ما التي مع أخطأتم ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع على إضمار مبتدأ

SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r1.claim: هو أقسط means naming them for their fathers; دعاؤهم is omitted, as in 5:8.
SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r1.anchor: أي: دعاؤهم لآبائهم، فأضمر المصدر لدلالة فعله عليه كقوله: اعدلوا هو أقرب [المائدة: 8].

SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r2.claim: ما may be genitive, coordinated with prior ما governed by في.
SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r2.anchor: أحدهما: أنها مجرورة المحل عطفا على " ما " قبلها المجرورة ب " في " ، والتقدير: ولكن الجناح فيما تعمدت.

SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r3.claim: Alternatively it is a nominative subject with omitted predicate: you are held accountable or liable.
SAMIN-DURR:33:5/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنها مرفوعة المحل بالابتداء، والخبر محذوف. تقديره: تؤاخذون به، أو عليكم فيه الجناح.

ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r5.anchor: هو أقسط عند الله) أي هو أعدل

ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r6.claim: If a person's father is unknown, treat him as a brother in religion if he believes, and call him brother.
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r6.anchor: فهو أخوك في الدين إذا كان مؤمنا

ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r7.claim: مواليكم may mean paternal cousins or allies in religion.
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r7.anchor: بنو عمكم، ويجوز أن يكون: ومواليكم

ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r8.claim: One analysis excuses mistakes before the rule and assigns sin to deliberate acts; ما is genitive and coordinated with the earlier ما.
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r8.anchor: قبل أن تنهوا عن هذا، ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم

ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r9.claim: The first ما is governed by في; on this analysis the next ما coordinates with it, contrasting mistakes and deliberate acts.
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r9.anchor: عطف على (ما) الأولى المعنى: وليس عليكم جناح

ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r10.claim: Alternatively, calling someone son is not blameworthy unless one intends to treat him as a child for inheritance.
ZAJJAJ:v4p214/r10.anchor: ولا جناح عليكم في أن تقولوا له با بني

ASAD-NOTES:33:5#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:33:5#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:33:5#n6/r1.claim: Naming adopted children by their real fathers makes their adoptive relationship clear and safeguards their true identity.
ASAD-NOTES:33:5#n6/r1.anchor: make it clear that your relationship is an adoptive one, and do not create the impression that they are your real children

ASAD-NOTES:33:5#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:33:5#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:33:5#n7/r1.claim: The excused mistake includes misattributing a child's parentage or affectionately calling the child one's son or daughter.
ASAD-NOTES:33:5#n7/r1.anchor: by making a mistake in the attribution of the child's parentage, or by calling him or her, out of love, "my son" or "my daughter"

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says there is no blame for calling someone by the wrong father when one believes that man is his father.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r3.anchor: قال قتادة لو دعوت رجلا لغير أبيه وأنت ترى أنه أبوه لم يكن عليك بأس

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r4.claim: ʿUmar distinguishes excused mistakes from intentional acts, saying forgiveness should be sought for deliberate sins.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r4.anchor: وسمع عمر بن الخطاب رجلا يقول اللهم اغفر لي خطاياي فقال استغفر الله للعمد فأما الخطأ فقد تجوز عنه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r5.claim: ʿUmar warns against deliberate wrongdoing, acquisitiveness, and thinking too highly of one's deeds rather than against mistakes, need, or undervaluing them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r5.anchor: وكان يقول ما أخاف عليكم الخطأ ولكني أخاف عليكم العمد وما أخاف عليكم العائلة ولكن أخاف عليكم التكاثر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r6.claim: Qatāda transmits the maxim that three things do not destroy a person: error, forgetfulness, and acts done under compulsion.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p111#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة وكان يقال ثلاث لا يهلك عليهن ابن آدم الخطأ والنسيان وما أكرهوا عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r1.claim: The command means to attribute the adopted children to their fathers and reserve their lineage for them.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that Zayd was called Zayd ibn Muḥammad until this verse came down, after which the Prophet named him Zayd ibn Ḥāritha ibn Sharāḥīl.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r2.anchor: أن زيد بن حارثة مولى رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ما كنا ندعوه إلا زيد بن محمد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r3.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts Zayd's capture, purchase for Khadīja, reunion with his family, and choice to remain with the Prophet, who freed and adopted him; Zayd was still called ibn Muḥammad until this command.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r3.anchor: أخرج إبن مردويه عن إبن عباس أنه كان في أخواله بني معن من بني ثعل من طي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r4.claim: The pronoun هو refers to the verbal noun implied by the command ادعوهم, as in the construction in 5:8.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r4.anchor: والضمير لمصدر أدعوا كما في قوله تعالى : ( أعدلوا هو أقرب للتقوى )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī reads أقسط as an absolute superlative from qist, meaning just: attributing them to their fathers is fully true and just in God's judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p147/r5.anchor: من القسط بمعنى العدل والمراد به البالغ

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r1.claim: Alternatively, أقسط retains its common comparative force: the attribution is more just than the false claim, described ironically as if it had some justice.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r1.anchor: وجوز أن يكون أفعل على ما هو الشائع فيه والمعنى أعدل مما قالوه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r2.claim: If you do not know or recognize their fathers, you cannot attribute the children to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r2.anchor: فإن لم تعلموا ( أي تعرفوا ( آباءهم ( فتنسبوهم إليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r3.claim: When their fathers are unknown, address them as brothers and allies in religion; after the verse, the formerly adopted Sālim was called Ḥudhayfa's client.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r3.anchor: أي وأولياؤكم فيه فأدعوهم بالأخوة والمولوية بتأويلهما بالأخوة والولاية في الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r4.claim: One interpretation takes مواليكم to mean your paternal cousins.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes the term to mean those you have freed or manumitted.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r6.claim: Religious kinship language is prescribed to comfort them; the verse does not limit address to their personal names.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r6.anchor: وكأن دعاءهم بذلك لتطييب قلبوهم ولذا لم يؤمر بدعائهم بأسمائهم فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r7.claim: One parsing makes ما تعمدت genitive, coordinated with ما أخطأتم; the objection is that nothing should separate a genitive conjunct from its governor, as in Sībawayh's example.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r7.anchor: على أن ( ما ) في محل الجر عطفا على ما من ( فيما أخطأتم )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that the coordination joins each relative pronoun together with its clause; alternatively, the phrase means but the deliberate act incurs sin, with ما as a nominative subject and an omitted predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r8.anchor: لأن المعطوف هو الموصول مع صلته أعني ما تعمدت على مثله

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r9.claim: Another parsing places ما in the nominative as a subject whose predicate is understood from context.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r9.anchor: ما في موضع رفع على الإبتداء وخبره جملة مقدرة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r10.claim: Attributing intention to the heart is a familiar construction, as in 2:283, where sin is attributed to the heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r10.anchor: ونسبة التعمد إلى القلوب على حد النسبة في قوله تعالى : ( فإنه آثم قلبه )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r11.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r11.claim: According to Mujāhid, error refers to what happened before the prohibition and deliberate conduct to what happened after it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r11.anchor: وفي الثاني بعده أخرجه الفريابي وإبن أبي شيبة وإبن جرير وإبن المنذر وإبن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r12.claim: Another view places both cases after the prohibition: there is no sin in accidentally calling someone else's child my son, but sin in doing so deliberately.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r12.anchor: وقيل : كلا الأمرين بعد النهي والخطأ مقابل العمد والمعنى لا إثم عليكم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r13.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r13.claim: Qatāda says there is no blame for calling a man by the wrong father when one believes that father is correct, but there is blame when one intends the misattribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148/r13.anchor: عن قتادة أنه قال في الآية : لو دعوت رجلا لغير أبيه وأنت ترى أنه أبوه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r1.claim: In a report from ʿĀʾisha, the Prophet says he fears deliberate wrongdoing for the community, not its mistakes.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r1.anchor: حديث عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إني لست أخاف عليكم الخطأ

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet's statement that mistake, forgetfulness, and coercion have been lifted from the community.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r2.anchor: وحديث إبن عباس قال : قال عليه الصلاة والسلام وضع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وماأكرهوا عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r3.claim: On a specific reading the clause excuses error in adoption; on a general reading it absolves error and not deliberate conduct, as the two reports also suggest.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r3.anchor: العفو عن الخطأ دون العمد على طريق العموم لحديث عائشة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r4.claim: On either reading, the clause is a parenthetical conclusion that reinforces obedience to the command while adding an independent ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r4.anchor: والجملة على تقديري الخصوص والعموم واردة على سبيل الإعتراض التذييلي تأكيدا لإمتثال ما نبدوا إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r5.claim: Some construe the clause as an implied command not to call adoptees your children deliberately; al-Ālūsī calls this unnecessary strain, whether the ruling is specific or general.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r5.anchor: وجعلها بعضهم عطفا مؤولا بجملة طلبية على معنى أدعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط لكم ولا تدعوهم لأنفسكم متعمدين

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r6.claim: The verse prohibits deliberate attribution according to the pagan practice of adoption; ordinary affectionate address such as an elder calling a child my son appears permissible.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r6.anchor: وظاهر الآية حرمة تعمد دعوة الإنسان لغير أبيه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r7.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r7.claim: Al-Khafājī says calling another's child one's son is discouraged because it imitates unbelievers, although figurative sonship can be valid like brotherhood.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r7.anchor: وفي حواشي الخفاجي على تفسير البيضاوي النبوة وإن صح فيها التأويل كالأخوة لكن نهى عنها بالتشبيه بالكفرة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī says al-Khafājī's note does not explain this verse's prohibition, which concerns pagan adoption; the sounder rationale is to block imitation of unbelievers altogether.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r8.anchor: ولعله لم يرد بهذا النهي ما تدل عليه الآية المذكورة فإن ما تدل عليه نهى التحريم عن الدعوة على الوجه الذي كان في الجاهلية

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r9.speaker: إبن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r9.claim: A report of Ibn Ḥajar's major legal opinions says it is disliked to call another person's child my son.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r9.anchor: حكاه لي من أرتضيه عن فتاوي إبن حجر الكبرى وحكم التبني بقوله

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r10.claim: If the person called one's son is one's enslaved person, the statement emancipates him; lineage is established only if he is of unknown lineage, could be the speaker's child, and was not previously attributed to another.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r10.anchor: إن كان عبدا للقائل العتق على كل حال ولا يثبت نسبه منه إلا إذا كان مجهول النسب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r11.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r11.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that adoption has no legal effect, establishing neither emancipation nor lineage.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r11.anchor: وعند الشافعي لا عبرة بالتبني فلا يفيد العتق ولا ثبوت النسب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r12.claim: For someone whose father is unknown, addressing him as brother or client appears equally permissible, though some forbid calling a sinner my client because it honors him.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r12.anchor: ثم الظاهر أنه لا فرق إذا لم يعرف الأب بين أن يقال ياأخي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r13.claim: Some prohibit calling a sinner my client, either on the basis of a report or because honoring him is forbidden; that rationale could also prohibit brotherly address when it honors a notable sinner.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r13.anchor: لكن صرح بعضهم بحرمة أن يقال للفاسق يامولاي لخبر في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r14.claim: Al-Ālūsī suggests that the permission to use brother or client for someone of unknown father may be limited to someone who is not sinful.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r14.anchor: فلعل الدعاء لغير معروف الأب بما ذكر مخصوص بما إذا لم يكن فاسقا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r15.claim: The command's form appears to make no distinction between male and female adoptees, although al-Ālūsī has found no known case of adopting girls in pre-Islamic practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r15.anchor: الظاهر أنه لا فرق في أمر الدعوة بين كون المدعو ذكرا وكونه إنثى لكن لم نقف على وقوع التبني للإناث في الجاهلية

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r16.claim: God forgives deliberate wrongdoing when the person repents, and in mercy lifts the blame from one who made a mistake.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r16.anchor: ولذا رفع سبحانه الجناح عن المخطيء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r17.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r17.claim: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ reports the Prophet's warning that anyone who knowingly claims a father other than his own is barred from Paradise; al-Ālūsī notes that some classify this as a major sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p148#2/r17.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : من إدعى إلى غير أبيه وهو يعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r1.claim: The two Ṣaḥīḥ collections also report that one who claims another father or client incurs God's, the angels', and all people's curse, and God accepts neither obligatory nor voluntary deeds from him.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r1.anchor: وأخرج الشيخان أيضا من إدعى إلى غير أبيه أو إنتمى إلى غير مواليه فعليه لعنة الله تعالى والملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r2.claim: Another report in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections says knowingly claiming another father is kufr.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r2.anchor: وأخرجا أيضا ليس من رجل إدعى لغير أبيه وهو يعلم إلا كفر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī's al-Ṣaghīr reports, through ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, his father, and his grandfather, that repudiating one's lineage or claiming an unknown lineage is kufr; al-Ālūsī grades the report ḥasan.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p149/r3.anchor: وحديثه حسن قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كفر من تبرأ من نسب وأن دق أو إدعى نسبا لا يعرف

ALUSI-FULL:v21p150/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p150/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p150/r7.claim: Al-Ṭībī links the declaration that God speaks truth to the preceding judgment that their claim has no reality, then reads the naming command through the surah's end as detailing the truth and straight path.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p150/r7.anchor: على هذه الفذلكة بجامع التضاد على منوال ما سبق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r1.claim: Adopted children should be called by the names of their biological fathers; this is more just before God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r1.anchor: {ادعوهم لآبائهم} الذين ولدوهم، {هو أقسط} أعدل، {عند الله}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r2.claim: Abdullah ibn Umar reports Zayd ibn Haritha saying that people used to call him Zayd ibn Muhammad until this verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر أن زيد بن حارثة مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ما كنا ندعوه إلا زيد بن محمد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r3.claim: When a child’s father is unknown, call the child a brother in religion; for freedmen who are not one’s sons, use the names of religious brothers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r3.anchor: إن كانوا محررين وليسوا ببنيكم، أي: سموهم بأسماء إخوانكم في الدين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r4.claim: An alternative meaning of “your clients” is your allies or guardians in religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r4.anchor: أولياءكم في الدين، {وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r5.claim: There is no blame for mistakenly assigning someone to a father other than his own before the prohibition; blame applies to deliberate misattribution after the prohibition.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r5.anchor: قبل النهي فنسبتموه إلى غير أبيه، {ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم} من دعائهم إلى غير آبائهم بعد النهي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r6.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r6.claim: Qatada defines the mistake as calling someone the son of a man while believing that man really is his father.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: "فيما أخطأتم به" أن تدعوه لغير أبيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p317#3/r7.claim: The “what” in “what your hearts intended” is genitive by coordination with the “what” in “in what you erred”; the sense is “but in what your hearts intended.”

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p318/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p318/r1.speaker: سعد، أبو بكرة، رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p318/r1.claim: Saʿd and Abu Bakra report the Prophet saying that anyone who knowingly claims descent from someone other than his father is barred from Paradise; the source identifies Saʿd as the first to shoot in God’s path and Abu Bakra as one who climbed the wall of Taif’s fortress.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p318/r1.anchor: فقالا سمعنا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r4.claim: Name adopted children after their fathers; this is the relevant part of the statements of truth mentioned above.

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r5.claim: The pronoun refers to the act of naming them after their fathers; aqsaṭ justifies that instruction, and the comparative form means greater truthfulness in an absolute sense.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r5.anchor: هو أقسط عند الله } تعليل له، والضمير لمصدر

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r6.claim: If their fathers are unknown, regard them as brothers in religion and allies, calling someone “my brother” or “my ally” in that sense.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r6.anchor: وأولياؤكم فيه فقولوا هذا أخي ومولاي بهذا التأويل

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r7.claim: There is no sin for mistaken attribution before the prohibition or later through forgetfulness or a slip of the tongue; liability attaches to what hearts intend.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r7.anchor: مخطئين قبل النهي أو بعده على النسيان أو سبق اللسان

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r8.claim: The omitted sense is either that sin attaches to what hearts deliberately intend, or that deliberate intention itself bears the sin.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r8.anchor: ولكن الجناح فيما تعمدت قلوبكم أو ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم فيه الجناح

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r9.claim: God is forgiving and merciful because He pardons the person who makes a mistake.

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r10.claim: In Bayḍāwī's school adoption has no legal effect; Abū Ḥanīfa holds that adopting a slave emancipates him and establishes lineage for an unknown child who could be attached to the adopter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r10.anchor: أن التبني لا عبرة به عندنا وعند أبي حنيفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r11.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds that adoption can establish the lineage of an unknown child if the child could be affiliated with the adopter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:4-5/r11.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة يوجب عتق مملوكه ويثبت النسب لمجهوله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p72/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p72/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p72/r7.claim: The Prophet had adopted Zayd, who was called Zayd ibn Muḥammad until the command to call adopted children by their fathers was revealed.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p72/r7.anchor: ما كنا ندعوه إلا زيد بن محمد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r4.claim: When their fathers are known, adopted children must be attributed to them; this is closer to justice than adoption, even when adoption arose from compassion, and this rule is central to the sūra’s coming events.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r4.anchor: أي أقرب إلى العدل من التبني

BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r5.claim: When their fathers are unknown from original or later ignorance, they are fellow believers if they joined the faith, and clients whether enslaved or freed; Sālim is an example.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r6.claim: The Prophet warned that whoever knowingly claims a father other than his own is barred from Paradise; al-Biqāʿī says al-Bukhārī and Muslim relate it from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and Abū Bakra.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r6.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( من ادعى إلى غير أبيه وهو يعلم فالجنة عليه حرام )

BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r7.claim: The no-blame clause reassures those anxious about earlier mistakes; “error” includes mistakes before or after the prohibition, including mistaken lineage and ẓihār.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r7.anchor: لما كانت عادتهم الخوف مما سبق من أحوالهم على النهي

BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r8.claim: The preposition “in” indicates error is wholly without sin; “by” might have suggested some sin remained but was merely forgiven.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r8.anchor: وعبر بالظرف ليعيد أن الخطأ لا إثم فيه بوجه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r9.claim: Only intentional action incurs guilt; this wording also removes blame for forgetfulness or a slip of the tongue after the prohibition.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r9.anchor: على سبيل النسيان أو سبق اللسان

BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r10.claim: Biqāʿī reads the feminine verb as implying that only a heart marked by “feminine softness” would deliberately do this after clarification.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r11.claim: He reads the plural of abundance as extending guilt broadly where deliberate conduct is not prohibited.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r11.anchor: ودل جمع الكثرة على عموم الإثم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r12.claim: God’s forgiveness covers the repentant sinner, while His mercy guides the returning errant and grants generosity.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p73/r12.anchor: من صفته الستر البليغ على المذنب النائب

DURR-FULL:v6p562/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p562/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p562/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports that people called Zayd ibn Haritha Zayd ibn Muhammad until this verse came down; the Prophet then named him Zayd ibn Haritha ibn Shurahbil.
DURR-FULL:v6p562/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر: أن زيد بن حارثة مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما كنا ندعوه إلا زيد بن محمد

DURR-FULL:v6p562/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p562/r2.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v6p562/r2.claim: Aisha's account says pre-Islamic adopters claimed and inherited their adopted sons. After the verse, adoptees were returned to known fathers, while the fatherless were treated as brothers in faith and clients; it recounts that the Prophet told Sahlah to nurse Salim so he would be unmarriageable to her.
DURR-FULL:v6p562/r2.anchor: عن عائشة أن أبا حذيفة بن عتبة بن ربيعة بن عتبة بن عبد شمس وكان ممن شهد بدرا تبنى سالما

DURR-FULL:v6p562/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p562/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p562/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts Zayd's capture among his maternal kin, sale at Ukaz, purchase by Hakim ibn Hizam for Khadija, transfer to the Prophet, and his upbringing in the Prophet's household.
DURR-FULL:v6p562/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كان من أمر زيد بن حارثة رضي الله عنه أنه كان في أخواله بني معن

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r1.claim: The continuation says that once the verse was revealed, Zayd was called by his biological father's name, Zayd ibn Haritha.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r1.anchor: حتى نزل القرآن {ادعوهم لآبائهم} فدعي زيد بن حارثة

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r2.speaker: الحسن بن عثمان
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r2.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Uthman reports from scholars that Amir ibn Rabi'a had been called Amir ibn al-Khattab; the verse was revealed concerning him, Zayd, Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfa, and al-Miqdad ibn Amr.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r2.anchor: من طريق زيد ابن شيبة عن الحسن بن عثمان رضي الله عنه قال: حدثني عدة من الفقهاء وأهل العلم

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r3.speaker: أبو بكرة
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r3.claim: Abu Bakra says he is among those whose father is unknown and is therefore one of the believers' brothers in religion.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r3.anchor: عن أبي بكرة رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r4.claim: Qatada glosses أقسط as more just before God.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله} أعدل عند الله

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r5.claim: Qatada says that when a person's father is unknown, he is a brother in religion and a client.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله} أعدل عند الله {فإن لم تعلموا

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says that if a person's father is unknown, he is a brother in religion and a client of so-and-so.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم} قال: إن لم تعرف أباه

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r7.speaker: مقاتل
