DURR-FULL:v6p564/r7.claim: Muqatil says that if fathers are unknown, people may be named as brothers in religion with names such as Abdullah or Abd al-Rahman, or called by their patron's name.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r7.anchor: عن مقاتل في الآية يقول: إن لم تعلموا لهم آياء تدعوهم إليهم فانسبوهم اخوانكم في الدين

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses the fallback status as a brother in religion and a client of Banu so-and-so.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم} يقول: أخوك في الدين ومولاك مولى بني فلان

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r9.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r9.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd says that when the verse came down, they did not know Salim's father; Salim was a client of Abu Hudhayfa and only their ally.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r9.anchor: عن سالم بن أبي الجعد قال: لما نزلت {ادعوهم لآبائهم} لم يعرفوا لسالم أبا ولكن مولى أبي حذيفة

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r10.claim: Mujahid says mistaken attribution occurred before the prohibition in this and other matters, whereas intentional attribution is culpable after the command and prohibition.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به} قال: هذا من قبل النهي في هذا وغيره

DURR-FULL:v6p564/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r11.claim: Qatada says there is no blame for calling someone by another father if one mistakenly believes that person is his father; blame attaches to deliberate intent.
DURR-FULL:v6p564/r11.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به} قال: لو دعوت رجلا لغير أبيه وأنت ترى أنه أبوه

IBNHIBBAN:4215/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r1.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r1.claim: Urwa reports that Abu Hudhayfa adopted Salim; after 33:5, adopted children were returned to known fathers, or treated as brothers in faith and clients when fathers were unknown.
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r1.anchor: أخبرني عروة بن الزبير أن أبا حذيفة بن عتبة بن ربيعة وكان من أصحاب رسول الله

IBNHIBBAN:4215/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r2.claim: When Sahla asked what to do now that adult Salim could no longer be treated as her natural son, the Prophet told her to nurse him five times, establishing milk kinship.
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r2.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أرضعيه خمس رضعات

IBNHIBBAN:4215/r3.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r3.claim: Aisha applied the adult-nursing instruction to men she wanted to admit to her presence, having her sister and nieces nurse them.
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r3.anchor: فأخذت بذلك عائشة فيمن كانت تحب أن يدخل عليها من الرجال

IBNHIBBAN:4215/r4.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r4.speaker: سائر أزواج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r4.claim: The Prophet's other wives held that adult nursing was a dispensation for Salim alone and refused to admit anyone on that basis.
IBNHIBBAN:4215/r4.anchor: وأبى سائر أزواج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يدخل عليهن بتلك الرضاعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r1.claim: The lām can mark affiliation or descent; the cited poetry and report show that it can make an explicit ‘daughter of’ unnecessary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r1.anchor: وفي حديث أبي قتادة : ( صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حاملا أمامة ابنة بنته زينب ولأبي العاص بن ربيعة ) فكانت اللام مغنية عن أن يقول وابنة أبي العاص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r2.speaker: أبو قتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r2.claim: Abu Qatada reports that the Prophet carried Umama, daughter of his daughter Zaynab and of Abu al-As ibn Rabiʿa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r2.anchor: وفي حديث أبي قتادة : ( صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حاملا أمامة ابنة بنته زينب ولأبي العاص بن ربيعة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r3.claim: The pronoun ‘he/it’ refers to the verbal noun implicit in the command: calling them by their fathers’ names.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r3.anchor: وضمير { هو أقسط عند الله } عائد إلى المصدر المفهوم من فعل { ادعوهم لآبائهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r4.claim: ‘He is more just’ is an explanatory resumption answering why adoptees should not be called after their adoptive parents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r4.anchor: وجملة { هو أقسط } استئناف بياني كأن سائلا قال : لماذا لا ندعوهم للذين تبنوهم ؟

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r5.claim: The comparative is absolute: calling them by their true fathers is full justice; the alternative wrongs both fathers and adoptees by erasing true lineage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r5.anchor: أي : هو قسط كامل وغيره جور على الآباء الحق والأدعياء ، لأن فيه إضاعة أنسابهم الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r6.claim: The explanation reinforces the prior rejection of adoption and reassures those attached to the old practice that this difficult rule comes from God’s care to end ignorance-era norms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r6.anchor: لتعلم عناية الله تعالى بإبطال أحكام الجاهلية في التبني ، ولتطمئن نفوس المسلمين من المتبنين والأدعياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r7.claim: If fathers are unknown, the verse insists on legitimate brotherhood or client affiliation rather than allowing old adoptive attribution; this preserves social closeness without its harm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r7.anchor: فجمع فيه تأكيدا للتشريع بعدم التساهل في بقاء ما كانوا عليه بعذر أنهم لا يعلمون آباء بعض الأدعياء ، وتأنيسا للناس أن يعتاضوا عن ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r8.claim: Salim, adopted by Abu Hudhayfa, was called Salim mawla Abu Hudhayfa; people continued to call al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad after his pre-Islamic adoption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r8.anchor: فصاروا يدعون سالما متبنى أبي حذيفة : سالما مولى أبي حذيفة ، وغيره ، ولم يشذ عن ذلك إلا قول الناس للمقداد بن عمرو : المقداد بن الأسود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r9.speaker: القرطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r9.claim: Al-Qurtubi says that after the verse was revealed, al-Miqdad declared, ‘I am al-Miqdad ibn ʿAmr,’ although the old name remained in circulation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r9.anchor: قال القرطبي : لما نزلت هذه الآية قال المقداد : أنا المقداد بن عمرو ، ومع ذلك بقي الإطلاق عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAshur questions al-Qurtubi’s assumption that continued use of al-Miqdad’s old name was deliberate: intention cannot be known, and habitual speech is plausibly an excused slip or forgetfulness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p261/r10.anchor: وفي قول القرطبي : ولو كان متعمدا ، نظر ، إذ لا تمكن معرفة تعمد من يطلق ذلك عليه . ولعله جرى على ألسنة الناس المقداد بن الأسود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r1.claim: ‘Your brothers’ predicates an omitted subject referring to the adoptees: they are at least Muslim brothers, or clients if they have client status.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r1.anchor: وارتفاع { إخوانكم } على الإخبار عن مبتدأ محذوف هو ضمير الأدعياء ، أي : فهم لا يعدون أن يوصفوا بالإخوان في الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r2.claim: The predicate naming adoptees as brothers or clients indirectly guides people to call them by one of those legitimate affiliations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r2.anchor: والإخبار بأنهم إخوان وموال كناية عن الإرشاد إلى دعوتهم بأحد هذين الوجهين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r3.claim: The waw divides alternatives and functions like ‘or’; people may choose brotherhood or, where applicable, client status, a legal easing for them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r3.anchor: والواو للتقسيم وهي بمعنى ( أو ) فتصلح لمعنى التخيير ، أي : فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فادعوهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r4.claim: The preposition ‘in’ is either figurative containment (brotherhood within religion) or indicates cause, as in being harmed for God and believers being brothers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r4.anchor: و { في } للظرفية المجازية ، أي : إخوانكم أخوة حاصلة بسبب الدين كما يجمع الظرف محتوياته ، أو تجعل { في } للتعليل والتسبب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r5.claim: Calling them brothers does not create the ambiguity of calling them sons: their brotherhood plainly means religious connection and consoles adoptees and their caregivers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r5.anchor: وليس في دعوتهم بوصف الأخوة ريبة أو التباس مثل الدعوة بالبنوة لأن الدعوة بالأخوة في أمثالهم ظاهرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r6.claim: Here ‘clients’ means allies by pact, not freedmen; alliance is analogous to religious brotherhood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r6.anchor: والمراد بالولاء في قوله { ومواليكم } ولاء المحالفة لا ولاء العتق ، فالمحالفة مثل الأخوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r7.claim: The verse abrogates the prior Muslim and Prophetic practice of naming adoptees after adoptive fathers: Qur’an abrogated practical and tacit Sunnah, the sense of saying adoption’s ruling was abrogated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p262/r7.anchor: وهذه الآية ناسخة لما كان جاريا بين المسلمين ومن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من دعوة المتبنين إلى الذين تبنوهم فهو من نسخ السنة الفعلية والتقريرية بالقرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p263/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p263/r1.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p263/r1.claim: Al-Tibi explains al-Kashshaf’s praise of the sūra’s sentence-linking: commands and matching justifications are arranged for emphasis, while separated clauses mark resumption and connected clauses signal contrast, through the discussion up to the Prophet’s precedence over believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p263/r1.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) : ( وفي فصل هذه الجمل ووصلها من الحسن والفصاحة ما لا يغبى عن عالم بطرق النظم ) . وبينه الطيبي فقال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p263/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p263/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p263/r2.claim: Because naming adoptees by their fathers is obligatory, the command also prohibits its opposite, except when it happens by mistake.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p263/r2.anchor: عطف على جملة { ادعوهم لآبائهم } لأن الأمر فيها للوجوب فهو نهي عن ضده لتحريمه كأنه قيل : ولا تدعوهم للذين تبنوهم إلا خطأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r1.claim: Since جناح means sin, the clause confirms that the command to call adoptees by their fathers is obligatory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r1.anchor: والجناح : الإثم ، وهو صريح في أن الأمر في قوله { ادعوهم لآبائهم } أمر وجوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r2.claim: Error covers habitual slips of the tongue in calling an adoptee a son; deliberate action is what belief and intention purposefully affirm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r2.anchor: ومعنى { فيما أخطأتم به } ما يجري على الألسنة خارجا مخرج الغالب فيما اعتادوه أن يقولوا : فلان ابن فلان للدعي ومتبنيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r3.claim: Adoption and saying ‘I adopted someone’ have no legal effect or status as a will; naming someone in a will to receive a son’s share is a bequest limited to one-third.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r3.anchor: إبطال حكم التبني وأن لا يقول أحد لدعيه : هو ابني ، ولا يقول : تبنيت فلانا ، ولو قاله أحد لم يكن لقوله أثر ولا يعتبر وصية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r4.claim: Abu Hanifa and his school establish filiation when a man claims an unknown-lineage person younger than himself as his son; if the person is his slave, he is also freed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r4.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه من قال : هو ابني ، وكان أصغر من القائل وكان مجهول النسب سنا ثبت نسبه منه ، وإن كان عبده عتق أيضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa says a claim that cannot biologically be true establishes no filiation but frees the claimant’s slave; his two companions disagree that the slave is freed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r5.anchor: وإن كان لا يولد مثله لمثله لم يثبت النسب ولكنه يعتق عليه عند أبي حنيفة خلافا لصاحبيه فقالا : لا يعتق عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r6.claim: A known-lineage person cannot acquire filiation through the claim; a slave is freed because the forbidden statement only means descent, whereas calling a slave ‘my brother’ does not free him if Islamic brotherhood is intended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r6.anchor: لأن ذلك يطلق في أخوة الإسلام بنص الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r7.claim: Calling an adoptee ‘my son’ affectionately is treated as a slip, but it should not be used casually when it could create suspicion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p264/r7.anchor: وإذا قال أحد لدعيه : يا بني ، على وجه التلطف فهو ملحق بالخطأ ولا ينبغي التساهل فيه إذا كانت فيه ريبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r1.claim: The command concerns adoptees, not biological grandchildren: the Prophet called al-Hasan his son and told people not to interrupt his son while urinating.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r1.anchor: وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحسن رضي الله عنه : ( إن ابني هذا سيد ) وقال : ( لا تزرموا ابني ) أي : لا تقطعوا عليه بوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r2.claim: The rule does not bar affectionate ‘my son’ address to someone who is not the speaker’s adoptee; people also call peers brother or sister.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r2.anchor: وكذلك لا يشمل ما يقوله أحد لآخر غير دعي له : يا ابني ، تلطفا وتقربا ، فليس به بأس لأن المدعو بذلك لم يكن دعيا للقائل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r3.speaker: الشاعر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r3.claim: A cited poetic line uses ‘my sister’ for a woman addressed as a peer, illustrating non-literal kinship address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر : أنتت أختي وأنت حرمة جاري وحرام علي خون الجوار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r4.speaker: النمر بن تولب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r4.claim: Al-Namir ibn Tawlab’s poem about women calling him their uncle is explained as their addressing him as ‘brother.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r4.anchor: قال النمر بن تولب : دعاني الغواني عمهن وخلتني لي اسم فلا أدعى به وهو أول يريد : أنهن كن يدعونه : يا أخي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r5.claim: The general negation excuses all accidental acts and is not restricted to the verse’s particular occasion; Qur’an 2:286 and the Prophetic report on error, forgetfulness, and coercion support this rule.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r5.anchor: وقوع { جناح } في سياق النفي ب { ليس } يقتضي العموم فيفيد تعميم انتفاء الإثم عن العمل الخطأ بناء على قاعدة عدم تخصيص العام بخصوص سببه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r6.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r6.claim: The Prophet says that error, forgetfulness, and coercion have been lifted from his community.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r6.anchor: وقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما أكرهوا عليه )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r7.claim: The command implicitly prohibits attributing someone to anyone but his father; a Prophetic report threatens such a person with God’s, angels’, and people’s curse and rejection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r7.anchor: ويفهم من قوله { ادعوهم لآبائهم } النهي عن أن ينسب أحد إلى غير أبيه بطريق لحن الخطاب . وفي الحديث : ( من انتسب إلى غير أبيه فعليه لعنة الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r8.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r8.claim: A Prophetic report curses whoever claims descent from someone other than his father and says God will not accept his deed or ransom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( من انتسب إلى غير أبيه فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين لا يقبل الله منه صرفا ولا عدلا )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r9.claim: Saying ‘you are my father and I am your son’ to honor or draw close is permissible when there is no confusion, as in Abu al-Tayyib’s line to Sayf al-Dawla.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r9.anchor: ويخرج من النهي قول الرجل لآخر : أنت أبي وأنا ابنك على قصد التعظيم والتقريب وذلك عند انتفاء اللبس ، كقول أبي الطيب يرقق سيف الدولة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r10.claim: God’s forgiveness and mercy explain why error incurs no sin: excusing it is an effect of His attributes toward creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p265/r10.anchor: تعليل نفي الجناح عن الخطأ بأن نفي الجناح من آثار اتصاف الله تعالى بالمغفرة والرحمة بخلقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r2.claim: لكن can reinforce by stating the contrary, as in 33:5, or clarify an earlier general negation, as in 33:40.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r2.anchor: إما لمجرد توكيد المعنى بذكر نقيضه مثل قوله تعالى : { وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به

MALIK:1284/r1.author: MALIK
MALIK:1284/r1.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
MALIK:1284/r1.claim: Urwa recounts Abu Hudhayfa's adoption of Salim, like the Prophet's adoption of Zayd; when 33:5 was revealed, adoptees were restored to their fathers or, if unknown, their mawlas.
MALIK:1284/r1.anchor: أخبرني عروة بن الزبير، أن أبا حذيفة

MALIK:1284/r2.author: MALIK
MALIK:1284/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MALIK:1284/r2.claim: In response to Sahla's concern that Salim still entered her home after adoption ended, the Prophet directs her to nurse him five times, establishing milk kinship.
MALIK:1284/r2.anchor: فقال لها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MALIK:1284/r3.author: MALIK
MALIK:1284/r3.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
MALIK:1284/r3.claim: Aisha applied the adult nursing dispensation beyond Salim, arranging for women in her family to nurse men she wanted to admit.
MALIK:1284/r3.anchor: فأخذت بذلك عائشة أم المؤمنين فيمن كانت تحب أن يدخل عليها من الرجال فكانت تأمر أختها أم كلثوم بنت أبي بكر الصديق

MALIK:1284/r4.author: MALIK
MALIK:1284/r4.speaker: سائر أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MALIK:1284/r4.claim: The other wives rejected Aisha's practice, treating the Prophet's instruction to Sahla as a special license for Salim alone.
MALIK:1284/r4.anchor: وأبى سائر أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r1.claim: Adopted sons must be addressed by biological fathers; when fathers are unknown, they are brothers in religion and allies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r1.anchor: أمر الله تعالى في هذه الآية بدعاء الأدعياء إلى آبائهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r2.speaker: الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r2.claim: People cited Zayd ibn Haritha and Salim, client of Abu Hudhayfa, among those addressed through adoptive lineage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r2.anchor: فقال الناس زيد بن حارثة وسالم مولى أبي حذيفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r3.speaker: أبو بكرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r3.claim: Al-Tabari says Abu Bakra recited the verse and said that, not knowing his father, he was the community’s brother and ally.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r3.anchor: أن أبا بكرة قرأ هذه الآية ثم قال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r4.speaker: الراوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r4.claim: The narrator adds that Abu Bakra would have claimed his father even if he learned the man was a donkey.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r4.anchor: قال الراوي: ولو علم والله أن أباه حمارا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r6.claim: Qatada says the Prophet warned that anyone knowingly claiming another man as his father is forbidden Paradise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: بلغنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r7.claim: The verse removes blame for mistaken, forgotten, or habitual attribution, while deliberate attribution remains blameworthy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r7.anchor: وليس عليكم جناح الآية رفع للحرج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r8.claim: God’s forgiveness concerns conduct before the prohibition; these attributes also apply generally.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r8.anchor: وكان الله غفورا رحيما يريد لما مضى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r9.claim: One group takes “their error” as earlier habit; Ibn Atiyya says this was not error before prohibition and here means forgetfulness or non-intent.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r10.claim: Qatada distinguishes sincerely believing someone is a man’s son from knowingly assigning him to a man other than his father.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r10.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن قتادة أنه قال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r11.claim: The penalty for mistake is lifted from this community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r11.anchor: والخطأ مرفوع عن هذه الأمة عقابه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r12.claim: The Prophet says mistake, forgetfulness, and coercion have been lifted from his community.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r13.claim: The Prophet says he does not fear forgetfulness for his community, but fears deliberate wrongdoing; the quotation continues on the next page.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p369/r13.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما أخشى عليكم النسيان. وإنما أخشى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r1.claim: Ibn Umar says they used to call Zayd ibn Haritha Zayd ibn Muhammad until this verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عمر ما كنا ندعو زيد بن حارثة إلا زيد بن محمد حتى نزلت أدعوهم لآبائهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى هو أقسط أي أعدل فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r3.claim: The phrase means if you do not know or recognize their fathers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r3.anchor: أي إن لم تعرفوا آباءهم فإخوانكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r4.claim: A suppressed subject is understood: they are your brothers, so one should address another as my brother.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r4.anchor: أي فهم إخوانكم فليقل أحدكم يا أخي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says mawālī here means your cousins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r5.anchor: ومواليكم قال الزجاج أي بنو عمكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj also allows mawālī to mean your allies in religion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مواليكم أولياءكم في الدين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r7.claim: Mujahid understands the pardon for mistaken attribution to cover what people said before the prohibition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r7.anchor: أحدها فيما أخطأتم به قبل النهي قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r8.claim: Qatada says the pardon covers calling someone by another father's name when one believes that attribution to be true.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r8.anchor: والثاني في دعائكم من تدعونه إلى غير أبيه وأنتم ترونه كذلك قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r9.speaker: حبيب بن أبي ثابت
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r9.claim: Habib ibn Abi Thabit takes the excused error to mean a lapse or forgetfulness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r9.anchor: والثالث فيما سهوتم فيه قاله حبيب بن أبي ثابت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r10.claim: Under Mujahid's view, deliberate acts mean misattribution after the prohibition; under Qatada's and Habib's views, they mean knowingly assigning a man to someone other than his father.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p351#2/r10.anchor: فعلى الأول يكون معنى قوله ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم أي بعد النهي وعلى الثاني والثالث ما تعمدت في دعاء الرجل إلى غير أبيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p376/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p376/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p376/r1.claim: The passage gives physical examples before its moral point: one person has one heart, a wife under zihar is not a mother, and an adopted person is not a biological son; 58:3 says mothers are those who gave birth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p376/r1.anchor: كما لا يكون للشخص الواحد قلبان في جوفه، ولا تصير زوجته التي يظاهر منها بقوله: أنت علي كظهر أمي أما له،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r1.claim: God abrogated the early Islamic allowance to claim unrelated adopted sons, commanding that their lineage be restored to their real fathers as the just course.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r1.anchor: هذا أمر ناسخ لما كان في ابتداء الإسلام من جواز ادعاء الأبناء الأجانب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reports that Zayd ibn Haritha was called Zayd ibn Muhammad until this verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر؛ أن زيدا بن حارثة مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ما كنا ندعوه إلا زيد بن محمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r4.claim: After the rule changed, God permitted marriage to an adopted son's former wife, exemplified by the Prophet's marriage to Zaynab, Zayd's wife.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r4.anchor: ولهذا لما نسخ هذا الحكم، أباح تعالى زوجة الدعي، وتزوج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بزينب بنت جحش زوجة (8)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r5.claim: The prohibition in 4:23 concerns sons from one's loins, so it excludes an adopted son who is not biologically descended.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r5.anchor: وقال في آية التحريم: {وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم} [النساء:23]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r11.claim: The affectionate address occurred at the Farewell Pilgrimage in year ten, after Zayd's death at Mu'ta in year eight, supporting the distinction from legal lineage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p377/r11.anchor: وهذا ظاهر الدلالة، فإن هذا كان في حجة الوداع سنة عشر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r1.claim: When the fathers are unknown, the adoptees are brothers in religion and clients; these bonds replace the lineage they lack.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r1.anchor: تعالى برد أنساب الأدعياء إلى آبائهم، إن عرفوا، فإن لم يعرفوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r2.claim: When Hamza's daughter followed the returning party from the Treaty of Hudaybiyya journey, Ali, Zayd, and Ja'far disputed who should care for her; the Prophet awarded her to her maternal aunt, Asma bint Umays.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r2.anchor: وتبعتهم ابنة حمزة تنادي: يا عم، يا عم. فأخذها علي وقال لفاطمة: دونك ابنة عمك فاحتمليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r3.claim: The Prophet ruled justly and satisfied each claimant, telling Zayd, whose lineage was unknown, that he was their brother and client as the verse says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r3.anchor: ففي هذا الحديث أحكام كثيرة من أحسنها: أنه، عليه الصلاة والسلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r4.speaker: أبو بكرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r4.claim: Abu Bakra said he did not know his father and counted himself among the Muslim brothers; his father remarked that he would have claimed even a donkey as father if he knew it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: حدثني يعقوب بن إبراهيم، حدثنا ابن علية، عن عيينة بن عبد الرحمن، عن أبيه قال: قال أبو بكرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r5.claim: A Prophetic report warns that knowingly claiming descent from someone other than one's father is disbelief.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r5.anchor: وقد جاء في الحديث: "من ادعى لغير أبيه، وهو يعلمه، كفر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r6.claim: There is no blame for mistakenly assigning someone to the wrong father after investigation and exertion; God removes the burden of error, as in the prayer of 2:286.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r6.anchor: إذا نسبتم بعضهم إلى غير أبيه في الحقيقة خطأ، بعد الاجتهاد واستفراغ الوسع؛ فإن الله قد وضع الحرج في الخطأ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r7.claim: In a Muslim report, God answers the believers' plea not to be taken to task for forgetfulness or error by saying, I have done so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r7.anchor: وثبت في صحيح مسلم أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "قال الله: قد فعلت"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r8.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r8.claim: The Prophet says a judge who exercises judgment and is right earns two rewards, while one who errs earns one; Ibn Kathir cites this for excusing honest error.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r8.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري، عن عمرو بن العاص قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا اجتهد الحاكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r9.claim: Another Prophetic report says God has lifted from the community liability for mistakes, forgetfulness, and acts done under compulsion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p378/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث الآخر: "إن الله رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان، وما يكرهون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r1.claim: Only deliberate falsehood incurs sin; Ibn Kathir links this to 2:225, where God distinguishes idle oaths from what hearts have earned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r1.anchor: أي: وإنما الإثم على من تعمد الباطل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r2.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r2.claim: Umar reports that revelation included the stoning verse and that the Prophet and the Muslims carried out stoning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن عمر أنه قال: بعث الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir cites an abrogated Quran wording that warned it was disbelief to disavow one's fathers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r3.anchor: وفي القرآن المنسوخ: "فإن (7) كفرا بكم أن ترغبوا عن آبائكم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r4.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r4.claim: Umar also reports the Prophet's warning not to exalt him as Christians exalted Jesus, but to call him God's servant and messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r4.anchor: وإن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا تطروني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r5.claim: A Prophetic hadith lists slandering lineage, wailing for the dead, and seeking rain through stars as three forms of disbelief among people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p379/r5.anchor: ورواه في الحديث الآخر: "ثلاث في الناس كفر: الطعن في النسب، والنياحة على الميت، والاستسقاء بالنجوم"

MUSNAD-AHMAD:25650/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25650/r1.speaker: عائشة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25650/r1.claim: Aisha relates that Abu Hudhayfa adopted Salim as the Prophet had adopted Zayd; she recalls that adopted sons had been called and inherited as sons until the verse restored known fathers and treated unknown parentage as brotherhood and clientage in faith.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25650/r1.anchor: عن عائشة، أن أبا حذيفة، تبنى سالما - وهو مولى لامرأة من الأنصار - كما تبنى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم زيدا

MUSNAD-AHMAD:25650/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25650/r2.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25650/r2.claim: In the report, the Prophet tells Sahla to nurse Salim five times, making him her son through foster kinship.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25650/r2.anchor: قالت: يا رسول الله كنا نرى سالما ولدا يأوي معي، ومع أبي حذيفة ويراني فضلا وقد أنزل الله عز وجل فيهم ما قد علمت

JISHUMI:v8p5700/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r1.claim: On the preceding legal question, Abū Ḥanīfa does not recognize the stated basis for establishing lineage; a person’s acknowledgment of an unknown-lineage child as his own is accepted as truthful and presumed to fit the marital bed.
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r1.anchor: يحمل على أنه صادق، وأنه ولد على فراشه؛ ولذلك لا يثبت في معروف النسب

JISHUMI:v8p5700/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r2.claim: Acknowledging paternity does not establish lineage for someone already known to have another lineage or older than the claimant; pre-Islamic adoption had been treated as birth, which revelation corrected.
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r2.anchor: ولذلك لا يثبت في معروف النسب ومن هو أكبر سنا منه، وكان أهل الجاهلية ينزلون التبني بمنزلة الولادة

JISHUMI:v8p5700/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r3.claim: Lineage may be known or unknown; not knowing it does not remove a believer’s religious brotherhood, which follows from holding faith.
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r3.anchor: ويدل قوله: (فإن لم تعلموا) الآية، أن النسب قد يعلم وقد يجهل، وأن جهالته لا تخرج المؤمن من الأخوة في الدين

JISHUMI:v8p5700/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r4.claim: The contrast between error and deliberate intent shows that lineage rulings allow for both mistaken and intentional attribution.
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r4.anchor: ويدل قوله: (فيما أخطأتم) أن أمر النسب لم يبن على اليقين؛ لذلك دخل فيه الخطأ والعمد

JISHUMI:v8p5700/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r5.claim: One answer says lineage is grounded in the established marital bed, to which attribution is attached.
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r5.anchor: قلنا: قيل: الفراش معلوم، والنسبة تتعلق به

JISHUMI:v8p5700/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r6.claim: Another answer grounds lineage in presumption unless established by a truthful report, evidence, or necessity; the Prophet’s descent to ʿAdnān and many Companions’ lineages are known necessarily.
JISHUMI:v8p5700/r6.anchor: وعلمنا نسب كثير من أصحابه ضرورة.

NASAI:3223/r1.author: NASAI
NASAI:3223/r1.speaker: عائشة
NASAI:3223/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that Abū Ḥudhayfa adopted Sālim and arranged his marriage; before the revelation, adopted sons were publicly treated as biological sons and inherited from their adopters.
NASAI:3223/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، أَنَّ أَبَا حُذَيْفَةَ بْنَ عُتْبَةَ

NASAI:3223/r2.author: NASAI
NASAI:3223/r2.speaker: الله
NASAI:3223/r2.claim: The revelation directs Muslims to identify adopted children by their fathers; when a father is unknown, they remain brothers in religion and mawālī rather than biological sons.
NASAI:3223/r2.anchor: حَتَّى أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي ذَلِكَ ‏{‏ ادْعُوهُمْ لآبَائِهِمْ هُوَ أَقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ

TIRMIDHI:3207/r3.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3207/r3.speaker: عائشة
TIRMIDHI:3207/r3.claim: Aisha glosses Zayd's blessings as Islam and emancipation; adopted Zayd, called ibn Muhammad, must be attributed to his father, while unknown fathers mean brother or client, the juster rule.
TIRMIDHI:3207/r3.anchor: عن عائشة، رضى الله عنها قالت لو كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كاتما شيئا من الوحي

TIRMIDHI:3207/r4.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3207/r4.speaker: author
TIRMIDHI:3207/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the narration gharīb and notes an alternate route through Masruq and Aisha that preserves only the shorter opening, not the full account.
TIRMIDHI:3207/r4.anchor: قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى هَذَا حَدِيثٌ غَرِيبٌ

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Haritha was adopted under the old custom; revelation ordered adopted sons affiliated to their fathers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r2.anchor: وكان زيد بن حارثة منهم قد تبناه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ما كان يصنع أهل الجاهلية

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r5.claim: Calling adopted children by their fathers ends assigning them to adopters as biological sons.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r6.claim: Ibn Umar says Zayd was called Zayd ibn Muhammad until the command to affiliate adoptees to their fathers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r6.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر ما كنا ندعو زيد بن حارثة إلا زيد بن محمد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r7.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r7.claim: The Prophet called Zayd by his father Haritha, whose family recognized and affirmed his lineage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r7.anchor: قال السدي فدعاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى حارثة وعرف كل نسبه فأقروا به

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r8.claim: More equitable means more just in speech and judgment before God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r8.anchor: أي أعدل عند الله قولا وحكما

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r9.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r9.claim: For unknown fathers, assign names used by brothers and clients, such as Abdullah or Abd al-Rahman.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r9.anchor: مثل عبد الله وعبيد الله وعبد الرحمن وعبد الرحيم وعبد العزيز , قاله مقاتل بن حيان

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r10.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r10.claim: Another view is to call such a person our brother or our client.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r10.anchor: الثاني : قولوا أخونا فلان وولينا فلان , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r11.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r11.claim: Companions compared their fathers; Salman called himself son of Islam and Umar affirmed this by calling himself Umar son of Islam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r11.anchor: وروى محمد بن المنكدر قال : جلس نفر من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r12.claim: If a father's identity is unknown, free people are brothers in faith and freed people are clients.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r12.anchor: الثالث : إنه إن لم يعرف لهم أب ينسبون إليه كانوا إخوانا إن كانوا أحرارا , وموالي إن كانوا عتقاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r13.claim: Al-Miqdad had been called al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth, but returned to affiliation with his father.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r13.anchor: فإن المقداد بن عمرو كان يقال له المقداد بن الأسود بن عبد يغوث الزهري فرجع إلى أبيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r14.claim: Sufyan ibn Ma'mar was claimed as Ma'mar's son; after conversion and Badr, he was affiliated to his father and Banu Zurayq.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r14.anchor: وسفيان بن معمر كانت أمه امرأة معمر في الجاهلية فادعاه ابنا ثم أسلم سفيان وشهد بدرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r15.claim: Salim had no known father and was affiliated through clientage to Abu Hudhayfa.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r15.anchor: وممن لم يعرف له أب سالم ، مولى أبي حذيفة ونسب إلى ولاء أبي حذيفة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r16.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r16.claim: The excused mistake occurred before prohibition; deliberate conduct after it is culpable.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r16.anchor: بعد النهي في هذا وغيره ، قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r17.speaker: حبيب بن أبي ثابت
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r17.claim: Mistake means forgetfulness, while what the heart intends is deliberate.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r17.anchor: ما قصدتموه عن عمد ، قاله حبيب بن أبي ثابت

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r18.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r18.claim: One excused mistake is calling someone by a name other than his father's.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r18.anchor: الثالث : ما أخطأتم به أن تدعوه إلى غير أبيه , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r19.claim: God forgives what occurred in pre-Islamic ignorance and accepts repentance in Islam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p371/r19.anchor: أي غفورا عما كان في الشرك , رحيما بقبول التوبة في الإسلام

MUJAHID:v2p513#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p513#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p513#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the exemption for mistakes concerns this and other matters before prohibition; deliberate wrongdoing is what someone does after clarification and prohibition.
MUJAHID:v2p513#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به ﴾ قال هذا قبل النهي في هذا وغيره ولكن ﴿ ما تعمدت قلوبكم ﴾ قال العمد ما أتى بعد البيان والنهي

MUQATIL:33:5/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:5/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:5/r1.claim: Call Zayd son of Haritha and do not affiliate him with another father.
MUQATIL:33:5/r1.anchor: قولوا زيد بن حارثة ولا تنسبوه إلى غير أبيه

MUQATIL:33:5/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:5/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:5/r2.claim: Aqsaṭ means more just in God's sight.
MUQATIL:33:5/r2.anchor: { هو أقسط } يعنى أعدل { عند الله }

MUQATIL:33:5/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:5/r3.speaker: زيد
MUQATIL:33:5/r3.claim: After the verse came down, Muslims called Zayd by his father; he replied that he was Haritha's son and his lineage was known.
MUQATIL:33:5/r3.anchor: فقال: زيد أنا بن حارثة معروف نسبى

MUQATIL:33:5/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:5/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:5/r4.claim: If Zayd's father is unknown, he remains the believers' brother in religion and their client.
MUQATIL:33:5/r4.anchor: فإن لم تعلموا لزيد أبا تنسبوه إليه، فهو أخوكم فى الدين

MUQATIL:33:5/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:5/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:5/r5.claim: Mawla here means a client, as in one person being the mawla of another.
MUQATIL:33:5/r5.anchor: فهو أخوكم فى الدين ومولاكم، يقول فلان مولى فلان

MUQATIL:33:5/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:5/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:5/r6.claim: There is no blame for mistakenly assigning Zayd another father before the prohibition.
MUQATIL:33:5/r6.anchor: { فيمآ أخطأتم به } قبل النهى ونسبوه إلى غير أبيه

MUQATIL:33:5/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:5/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:5/r7.claim: Blame applies to intentional misattribution after the prohibition.
MUQATIL:33:5/r7.anchor: { ولكن } الجناح فى { ما تعمدت قلوبكم } بعد النهى

MUQATIL:33:5/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:5/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:5/r8.claim: God forgives their earlier calling Zayd son of Muhammad and is merciful afterward.
MUQATIL:33:5/r8.anchor: غفورا لما كان من قولهم من قبل أن زيد بن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم رحيما فيما بقى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r1.claim: Calling adopted children by their fathers' names is more just and fair in God's sight, the more equitable alternative.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r1.anchor: ﴿ ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط ﴾ أعدل ﴿ عند الله ﴾ وبين أن دعاءهم لآبائهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r2.claim: In pre-Islamic custom, a man who liked another's son adopted him, gave him a son's inheritance share, and called him by his own lineage.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r2.anchor: كان الرجل فى الجاهلية إذا أعجبه ولد الرجل ضمه إلى نفسه وجعل له مثل نصيب الذكر من أولاده من ميراثه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r3.claim: The eloquence comes from alternating connection and separation among imperative, declarative, nominal, then imperative clauses.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r3.anchor: حيث وصل الجملة الطلبية فصل الخبرية عنها ووصل بيها ثم فصل الاسمية عنها ووصل بينها ثم فصل بالطلبية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r4.claim: If their fathers are unknown, there is no father to whom they can be attributed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r4.anchor: فإن لم تعلموا لهم آباء تنسبونهم اليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r5.claim: They are brothers and allies in religion; calling someone brother or mawla refers to religious kinship and alliance.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r5.anchor: فهم إخوانكم فى الدين وأولياؤكم فى الدين فقالوا هذا أخى وهذا مولاى ويا أخى ويامولاى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r6.claim: Mistaken attribution through ignorance before prohibition is not sinful; deliberate attribution afterward is. The rule covers adoption error and intent.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r6.anchor: أى لا اثم عليكم فيما فعلتموه من ذلك مخطئين جاهلين قبل ورود النهى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r7.claim: ما in the second clause may be genitive, coordinated with the earlier ما.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r7.anchor: وما فى موضع الجر عطف على ما الأولى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r8.claim: For an adoptee of unknown lineage younger than the adopter, lineage is established and an enslaved person freed; if older, lineage is not established but emancipation still occurs.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r8.anchor: وإذا وجد التبنى فان كان المتبنى مجهول النسب وأصغر سنامنه ثبت نسبه منه وعتق ان كان عبدا له وان كان أكبر سنامنه لم يثبت النسب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r9.claim: Adoption cannot establish lineage for someone of known lineage, though an enslaved adoptee is freed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r9.anchor: وأما المعروف النسب فلا يثبت نسبه بالتبنى وعتق ان كان عبدا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r10.claim: God does not hold people accountable for mistakes and accepts repentance from those who acted deliberately.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p296/r10.anchor: لا يؤاخذكم بالخطأ ويقبل التوبة من المتعمد

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5/r6.speaker: أنس بن مالك وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5/r6.claim: A report says Zayd was captured in Syria by raiders from Tihama, bought by Hakim ibn Hizam, given to Khadija, then given to Muhammad, who freed and adopted him; when his father and uncle came seeking ransom, Zayd chose to stay, and Muhammad publicly declared him his son and heir.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5/r6.anchor: وكان زيد فيما روي عن أنس بن مالك وغيره مسبيا من الشام، سبته خيل من تهامة

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r1.claim: The verse concerning Zayd ended adoption as a recognized basis for inheritance and mutual support, and directs people to the known biological father as the more just attribution.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r1.anchor: وفي قول ابن عمر: ما كنا ندعو زيد بن حارثة إلا زيد بن محمد، دليل على أن التبني كان معمولا به

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r2.claim: In pre-Islamic practice, a man might adopt someone whose appearance or character pleased him, grant him a son's share of inheritance, and call him his son.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r2.anchor: كان الرجل في الجاهلية إذا أعجبه من الرجل جلده وظرفه ضمه إلى نفسه، وجعل له نصيب الذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r3.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r3.claim: Al-Nahhas calls the verse abrogation of the former adoption practice, a case of Qur'an abrogating Sunna: use the known father, otherwise known patronal affiliation, and otherwise brotherhood in religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r3.anchor: وقال النحاس: هذه الآية ناسخة لما كانوا عليه من التبني، وهو من نسخ السنة بالقرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r4.claim: There is no sin when the tongue mistakenly gives someone an adoptive father's name; Qatada also exempts addressing someone as another's son when one believes that man is his father.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r4.anchor: لو نسبه إنسان إلى أبيه من التبني فإن كان على جهة الخطأ، وهو أن يسبق لسانه إلى ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r5.claim: Qatada says mistakenly calling a man the son of someone believed to be his father is covered by the verse's lifting of blame.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r5.anchor: قاله قتادة. ولا يجري هذا المجرى ما غلب عليه اسم التبني

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r6.claim: Established names from prior adoption continued for people such as al-Miqdad ibn Amr, known as Ibn al-Aswad, and Salim mawla Abi Hudhayfa; Qurtubi distinguishes them from Zayd, whom one may not deliberately call Zayd ibn Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r6.anchor: فإن الأسود بن عبد يغوث كان قد تبناه في الجاهلية وعرف به. فلما نزلت الآية قال المقداد

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r7.claim: Deliberately calling Zayd ibn Haritha “Zayd ibn Muhammad” is sinful; Qurtubi reads God as forgiving deliberate wrong and merciful by removing the penalty for accidental error.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r7.anchor: فإن قاله أحد متعمدا عصى لقوله تعالى: { ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم } أي فعليكم الجناح

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r8.speaker: عطاء وكثير من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r8.claim: A group including Ata treats the clause broadly: one who swears not to leave a creditor until paid, accepts coins thought good, and then finds them counterfeit bears no liability.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#2/r8.anchor: وكانت فتيا عطاء وكثير من العلماء. على هذا إذا حلف رجل ألا يفارق غريمه حتى يستوفي منه حقه

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r1.claim: Under the broad reading of accidental error, someone who swears not to greet a person but greets him unknowingly has not broken the oath.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r1.anchor: وكذلك عنده إذا حلف ألا يسلم على فلان فسلم عليه وهو لا يعرفه أنه لا يحنث

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r2.claim: The second “ma” may be genitive by coordination with the first “ma”; alternatively it is nominative after an implied subject, “what you are answerable for is what your hearts intended.”
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r2.anchor: و«ما» في موضع خفض ردا على «ما» التي مع «أخطأتم». ويجوز أن تكون في موضع رفع

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r3.speaker: قتادة وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r3.claim: Qatada and others say that mistakenly attributing a man to someone believed to be his father is among the errors for which God removed blame; another view is simply addressing someone as “my son” without adopting him.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r3.anchor: قال قتادة وغيره: من نسب رجلا إلى غير أبيه، وهو يرى أنه أبوه، خطأ فذلك من الذي رفع الله

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r7.claim: Adiya is the plural of da'i, someone called the son of a man other than his father or claiming someone other than his father; the verbal noun is da'wa, with a kasra. Unknown lineage makes one a patron and brother in religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r7.anchor: الأدعياء جمع الدعي، وهو الذي يدعى ابنا لغير أبيه أو يدعي غير أبيه والمصدر الدعوة بالكسر

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r8.speaker: أبو بكرة
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r8.claim: Al-Tabari reports Abu Bakra reading the verse and saying that, since his father was unknown, he was the Muslims' brother in religion and patron; the narrator says Abu Bakra would have claimed even a donkey as father if he knew it. Hadith transmitters call him Nufay ibn al-Harith.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r8.anchor: وذكر الطبري أن أبا بكرة قرأ هذه الآية وقال: أنا ممن لا يعرف أبوه، فأنا أخوكم في الدين

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r9.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وأبو بكرة
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r9.claim: A report in the Sahih collections, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Abu Bakra, says the Prophet declared Paradise forbidden to one who knowingly claims a father other than his own.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r9.anchor: روى الصحيح عن سعد بن أبي وقاص وأبي بكرة كلاهما قال: سمعته أذناي ووعاه قلبي محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r10.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r10.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying that a man who knowingly claims a father other than his own commits disbelief; Qurtubi gives no grading here.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:5#3/r10.anchor: وفي حديث أبي ذر أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:
